text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Plain-clothed security agents posted to airports to forestall any acts of sabotage, witnesses said.
- The study of French language may become compulsory in all Nigerian schools if government implements report of panel on higher education.

- Association of Nigerian oil explorers urges government to enter into dialogue with multinational oil producers in the country over issue of farming out marginal oil wells to indigenous firms to exploit.
- Sale of government enterprises such as power and telecoms in the New Year will boost stock market capitalisation by more than 55.6 billion naira, operators say.
- Food prices remain stable six days after Christmas as traders complain of lack of buyers, market survey shows.
- Ban on trading in shares of ADC airlines, whose aircraft crashed in November killing all 143 on board, will soon be lifted.
- Shell oil company executive says gas flaring will be a thing of the past in Nigeria by year 2000.
- External debt worth $166.6 million redeemed through debt conversion programme in 1996.
- Political sources say military ruler General Sani Abacha has told his ministers not to become involved in activities of five political parties registered to vie for power in 1998.
